items.followUp: Write two differences between a molecule and an ion.

rubric.why: An atom is electrically neutral, while an ion carries a positive or negative charge.
rubric.description: Contrasts the electrical charges of an atom and an ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating that an atom is neutral and an ion is charged.

rubric.why: Atoms have equal numbers of protons and electrons; ions form when electrons are lost or gained.
rubric.description: Gives a second difference based on electron count or ion formation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons, or that an ion forms by losing or gaining electrons.

modelAnswer: An atom is electrically neutral, whereas an ion has a positive or negative charge.
An atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons; an ion forms when an atom loses or gains electrons.

rubric.why: The lanthanide series consists of fourteen elements.
rubric.description: States the number of elements in the lanthanide series.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the series as consisting of fourteen elements.

rubric.why: The lanthanides extend from cerium to lutetium and follow lanthanum in the periodic table.
rubric.description: Identifies the range of the series or its position after lanthanum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the range from cerium to lutetium or stating that the elements follow lanthanum.

modelAnswer: Lanthanides are the fourteen elements from cerium (Ce) to lutetium (Lu).
They follow lanthanum in Period 6 of the periodic table.

items.followUp: Why does ionization energy generally increase across a period?

rubric.why: Atomic size and shielding increase down a group, increasing the distance between the outer electron and the nucleus.
rubric.description: States that atomic size or shielding increases down the group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying an increase in atomic size, atomic radius, or shielding down the group.

rubric.why: The outer electron is less strongly attracted to the nucleus, so less energy is needed to remove it.
rubric.description: Explains that weaker attraction to the outer electron lowers the energy required to remove it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking weaker nuclear attraction to less energy being required to remove an electron.

modelAnswer: Down a group, atomic size and the shielding effect increase.
The outer electron is farther from the nucleus and is less strongly attracted, so less energy is required to remove it.
